report.headline: RRP peaked at 478.08045 $/MWh for interval ending 2026-07-31 07:30 AEST (2026-07-30T21:30:00Z).
summary: Five-minute RRP peak: 478.08045 $/MWh, interval end 2026-07-31 07:30 AEST (evidence: ev0442).
Dispatch TOTALDEMAND at the peak interval was 1472.42 MW (evidence: ev0443).
Operational demand for the half-hour ending 2026-07-30T21:30:00Z was 1402.0 MW (evidence: ev0905); the window maximum operational demand was 1455.0 MW (evidence: ev0906).
Net interchange at the peak interval was 382.68 MW net flow out of TAS1 (evidence: ev0444).
There were 12 five-minute intervals at-or-above the $300.0/MWh analysis threshold in the window (evidence: ev0878; threshold evidence: ev0880).
Hobart hourly modelled temperature reached a minimum of 6.49 °C at 2026-07-30T21:00:00Z (evidence: ev0942).
SCADA observations show notable generation changes in the surrounding window (examples: GORDON +93.33 MW ev0982; CETHANA +59.22 MW ev0985; CTHLWF −12.43 MW ev0994).
retrieve_public_evidence searched notices for TAS1 and the event window and returned no market notice held for this region and window (retrieve_public_evidence search_scope outcome).

possible_explanations.statement: Lower temperatures in Hobart around 2026-07-30T21:00:00Z (ev0942) might have increased regional electrical heating load and thus contributed to higher operational demand at 2026-07-30T21:30:00Z (ev0905, ev0443).
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Compare half-hourly temperatures across Tasmanian weather reference locations (e.g. Southern Tasmania Hobart [c2]) with operational demand at 2026-07-30T21:30:00Z and the historical temperature–demand responsiveness for those locations.

possible_explanations.statement: Large net exports and a tightened local supply margin might have coincided with the spike (net interchange +382.68 MW at 2026-07-30T21:30:00Z, ev0444; dispatch TOTALDEMAND 1472.42 MW at 2026-07-30T21:30:00Z, ev0443).
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Inspect interconnector availability, interconnector offer/dispatch records and constraint binding for 2026-07-30T21:30:00Z (2026-07-31 07:30 AEST (UTC+1000)) and compare offer stacks and available local generation at those times.

possible_explanations.statement: Rebids or high-priced offers from market participants could have produced the spike independent of temperature and demand patterns (see surrounding generator SCADA changes such as GORDON +93.33 MW ev0982 and CETHANA +59.22 MW ev0985).
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Obtain offer and rebid histories and the dispatch offer stack for 2026-07-30T21:20:00Z through 2026-07-30T21:35:00Z (UTC) and check for high-priced offers or rebids covering the interval ending 2026-07-30T21:30:00Z (2026-07-31 07:30 AEST (UTC+1000)).

citations.quote: The major factors considered in the statistical models are: • Temperature profile • Weather season • Week day / weekend • Unusual conditions (school / public holidays / daylight savings)
citations.supports: AEMO procedure lists temperature profile as a major factor in short-term load forecasting.
AEMO load-forecasting procedure uses Hobart as the weather reference location for Southern Tasmania.

uncertainties: The weather context is a model-derived hourly point for Hobart (ev0942/ev0949) and may not represent temperatures across all Tasmanian load centres.
Generation change results are descriptive SCADA observations and do not by themselves show offers, outages or bidding behaviour (generation_change tool caveat).
Dispatch TOTALDEMAND (5-minute dispatch measure, ev0443) and operational demand (30-minute measured series, ev0905/ev0906) are different measures and should not be conflated without care.
